Completed a bounded continuation across all eight chapters. No score or ranking was produced.

The environment remained read-only, so I could not update `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following globally new records should be appended, preserving their exact `methodology_ids`:

- `WEB-1B-13` — Presidential ordinance created the Conseil National de Cyberdéfense in 2023, establishing a specialized cyber-defense institution. Supports implementation, not effectiveness. Lenses: `1B.1`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`. [Presidential cyber strategy](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/la_strategie_nationale_de_cybersecurite), [DRC digital-code text](https://are.gouv.cd/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/04042023-ORDONNANCE-LOI-23-010-DU-13-MARS-PORTANT-CODE-DU-NUMERIQUE_compressed.pdf).

- `WEB-1B-14` — The digital-code claim is recoverable through the official ordinance-law PDF, correcting `WEB-1B-05`’s mismatched URL. The code covers cybercrime, cryptology, electronic evidence, and digital governance. Lenses: `1B.1`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`. `WEB-1B-05` should be replaced or dispositioned as superseded.

- `WEB-1B-15` — UNJHRO documented 5,273 human-rights violations and abuses in 2023, a 12% national decrease from 2022, while conflict provinces remained heavily affected. Mixed outcome context, not proof of presidential effectiveness. Lenses: `1B.8`, `1B.10`. [MONUSCO/UNJHRO](https://monusco.unmissions.org/en/actualites/principales-tendances-des-violations-des-droits-de-lhomme-en-rdc-1er-janvier-au).

- `WEB-2B-12` — UN document `S/2023/904` confirms the 21 November 2023 MONUSCO disengagement agreement and withdrawal framework, replacing summary-only locators. Lenses: `2B.1`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [UN document](https://documents.un.org/api/symbol/access?l=en&s=s%2F2023%2F904&t=pdf).

- `WEB-2B-13` — Resolution 2717 required gradual withdrawal tied to civilian-protection safeguards and warned against security gaps. It establishes negotiated transition, not improved security. Lenses: `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [Resolution 2717](https://monusco.unmissions.org/sites/default/files/res_2717_2023_n2341267_en_0.pdf).

- `WEB-3B-07` — UNJHRO’s 2023 totals provide a mixed line: national documented abuses declined, but conflict provinces retained severe exposure. Lenses: `3B.1`, `3B.6`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`. [UNJHRO trends](https://monusco.unmissions.org/en/actualites/principales-tendances-des-violations-des-droits-de-lhomme-en-rdc-1er-janvier-au).

- `WEB-4B-08` — The original CENCO-ECC declaration is available and should replace secondary summaries for observer findings. Lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [CENCO-ECC declaration](https://cencordc.org/attachments/article/416/VF_D%C3%A9claration_MOE_CENCO-ECC_2023.pdf).

- `WEB-4B-09` — Carter Center’s final report independently documents technical and procedural election problems, including delayed openings, electronic-voting issues, and official turnout of 42.65%. Lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.6`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [Carter Center report](https://www.cartercenter.org/resources/pdfs/news/peace_publications/election_reports/drc/drc-final-report-2023.pdf).

- `WEB-5B-09` — The Ministry of Budget provides primary 2023 budget and execution documents, including June and December execution reports. This is a recovery path for expenditure-quality claims; it does not itself establish effective spending. Lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`. [Budget 2023 portal](https://budget.gouv.cd/budget-2023/), [December execution report](https://budget.gouv.cd/wp-content/uploads/execution/esb2023/decembre/commentaires.pdf).

- `WEB-6B-09` — The available evidence indicates no nationally representative household survey for 2023; later survey work is described as the first nationwide survey in more than a decade. Distributional welfare claims therefore remain evidence-limited. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.10`. [Joint Data Center](https://www.jointdatacenter.org/drc-household-living-conditions-survey/).

- `WEB-7B-06` — The primary CENCO-ECC material strengthens institutional election-integrity evidence but still does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal enrichment, concealment, or direct manipulation. Lenses: `7B.1`, `7B.2`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.8`, `7B.10`.

- `WEB-8B-07` — A March 2023 government implementation meeting reported PDL-145T preparation activity and a phone-based public tracking mechanism. This supports administrative machinery and monitoring, not completed works or beneficiary outcomes. Lenses: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`. [Primature](https://www.primature.gouv.cd/2023/03/11/programme-de-developpement-local-des-145-territoires-les-premiers-ouvrages-vont-etre-livres-des-le-mois-davril-selon-les-rapports-de-differentes-agences-dexecution-remis-au-premier-ministre-sam/).

Additional targeted findings:

- PDL-145T received adverse implementation scrutiny: CREFDL called for audits after reporting that no school, health center, or administrative building had been completed in certain reviewed areas. This is a promising `8B` contrary-evidence unit, but the underlying report should be opened and precisely located before assigning a new ledger ID. [7sur7 coverage](https://7sur7.cd/2023/12/19/programme-de-145-territoires-aucune-ecole-aucun-centre-de-sante-ou-batiment).

- The Ministry of Budget’s execution documents provide a stronger primary path for `5B`, including military and general expenditure tables, but they do not by themselves establish procurement quality, leakage, or household benefit.

- Searches for personal asset declarations, conflicts of interest, beneficial ownership, and adjudicated personal enrichment produced no defensible 2023 ruler-specific finding. Chapter `7B` therefore remains institutionally documented but personally underdetermined.

The recoverable research gaps are now narrower: verified cyber and PDL-145T outcomes, expenditure-quality audits, personal-integrity records, and representative welfare data.
